title: Semantic Record
description: CoALA semantic memory: what is true. Facts about the world, the user, and the agent itself — distilled from episodes or asserted directly. Unlike an episode, a semantic record is timeless in form but not in validity: it carries a validity window and can be contradicted or superseded.

subject.description: Optional triple form. When present, enables exact-match lookup and mechanical contradiction detection (same subject+predicate, different object). When absent, the fact lives only in `content` and contradictions must be found semantically.

valid_from.description: When this fact started being true. Distinct from created_at, which is when the agent learned it.

valid_to.description: When this fact stopped being true. Null means still valid. A record with valid_to in the past is excluded from recall by default but retained — knowing a fact used to be true is itself useful.

contradicts.description: Records this fact is in tension with. Populated by the reflection pass. Presence of a contradiction does NOT auto-resolve anything: both records stay active and recall surfaces the conflict, because silently picking a winner is how a memory store starts lying.

corroborations.description: Number of independent episodes that support this fact. Reflection raises confidence as this grows; a fact seen once is not a fact seen often.

volatility.description: How fast this class of fact goes stale, which sets the default TTL and how aggressively reflection rechecks it. A phone number is stable; a project status is volatile.

sensitivity.description: Drives redaction policy. Records marked 'pii' or 'secret' are excluded from context_block by default and are the first targets of a memory_forget redaction sweep. 'secret' should never have been written here in the first place — the flag exists so it can be found and removed.
